      "textSnapshot": "Problem: The install and onboarding experience for entire-brain was fragmented. The main README and documentation focused only on installation (getting plugins onto a machine) while leaving users uncertain about the next step: how to actually onboard a repository and get a usable brain. Users had to discover entire brain setup as a secondary option, and the documentation did not make clear what prerequisites it needed, what it costs in tokens, what services it installs, or how to control those installations.\nSolution: This branch centralizes the journey around the realistic endpoint—a brain actively working in a user's repository—and breaks it into two clearly-sequenced commands:\nMachine install (scripts/install.sh): Builds and registers two plugins. No repository-specific setup. The README now opens with both commands and states plainly that installing gives no repository a brain.\nRepository onboarding (entire brain setup): A single command that runs in three phases—instant deterministic core (free, seconds), optional fact backfill (token spend, detached, capped at 25 sessions by default), and optional persistent watcher daemon (recurring token spend, launchd agent on macOS / systemd user unit on Linux, installed by default without a prompt).\nThe branch adds four new demo/test scripts and comprehensive documentation clarifying what setup requires (a local git repo, nothing else), what it degrades around (missing entire enable, no captured sessions, no provider), token spend gates and defaults, and paths for both learning (trial-setup.sh, demo-setup.sh, demo-agent-session.sh) and scripting (--no-backfill, --no-daemon). It fixes first-run bugs (JSON parse failures from version banners, missing semantic provider errors, dirty-worktree refusals) and daemon lifecycle issues (duplicate distillation, concurrent setup races, double distillation on re-run). The status command gains an Onboarding section showing backfill progress and watcher health, and the daemon's token spend is now properly gated on per-repo watch cursors instead of a once-per-process budget that would never reset on a long-lived service.",

      "textSnapshot": "Problem: The install and onboarding experience for entire-brain was fragmented. The main README and documentation focused only on installation (getting plugins onto a machine) while leaving users uncertain about the next step: how to actually onboard a repository and get a usable brain.   "body": "Problem: The install and onboarding experience for entire-brain was fragmented. The main README and documentation focused only on installation (getting plugins onto a machine) while leaving users uncertain about the next step: how to actually onboard a repository and get a usable brain. Users had to discover entire brain setup as a secondary option, and the documentation did not make clear what prerequisites it needed, what it costs in tokens, what services it installs, or how to control those installations.\nSolution: This branch centralizes the journey around the realistic endpoint—a brain actively working in a user's repository—and breaks it into two clearly-sequenced commands:\nMachine install (scripts/install.sh): Builds and registers two plugins. No repository-specific setup. The README now opens with both commands and states plainly that installing gives no repository a brain.\nRepository onboarding (entire brain setup): A single command that runs in three phases—instant deterministic core (free, seconds), optional fact backfill (token spend, detached, capped at 25 sessions by default), and optional persistent watcher daemon (recurring token spend, launchd agent on macOS / systemd user unit on Linux, installed by default without a prompt).\nThe branch adds four new demo/test scripts and comprehensive documentation clarifying what setup requires (a local git repo, nothing else), what it degrades around (missing entire enable, no captured sessions, no provider), token spend gates and defaults, and paths for both learning (trial-setup.sh, demo-setup.sh, demo-agent-session.sh) and scripting (--no-backfill, --no-daemon). It fixes first-run bugs (JSON parse failures from version banners, missing semantic provider errors, dirty-worktree refusals) and daemon lifecycle issues (duplicate distillation, concurrent setup races, double distillation on re-run). The status command gains an Onboarding section showing backfill progress and watcher health, and the daemon's token spend is now properly gated on per-repo watch cursors instead of a once-per-process budget that would never reset on a long-lived service.",

Users had to discover entire brain setup as a secondary option, and the documentation did not make clear what prerequisites it needed, what it costs in tokens, what services it installs, or how to control those installations.\nSolution: This branch centralizes the journey around the realistic endpoint—a brain actively working in a user's repository—and breaks it into two clearly-sequenced commands:\nMachine install (scripts/install.sh): Builds and registers two plugins. No repository-specific setup. The README now opens with both commands and states plainly that installing gives no repository a brain.\nRepository onboarding (entire brain setup): A single command that runs in three phases—instant deterministic core (free, seconds), optional fact backfill (token spend, detached, capped at 25 sessions by default), and optional persistent watcher daemon (recurring token spend, launchd agent on macOS / systemd user unit on Linux, installed by default without a prompt).\nThe branch adds four new demo/test scripts and comprehensive documentation clarifying what setup requires (a local git repo, nothing else), what it degrades around (missing entire enable, no captured sessions, no provider), token spend gates and defaults, and paths for both learning (trial-setup.sh, demo-setup.sh, demo-agent-session.sh) and scripting (--no-backfill, --no-daemon). It fixes first-run bugs (JSON parse failures from version banners, missing semantic provider errors, dirty-worktree refusals) and daemon lifecycle issues (duplicate distillation, concurrent setup races, double distillation on re-run).       "textSnapshot": "Problem: The install and onboarding experience for entire-brain was fragmented. The main README and documentation focused only on installation (getting plugins onto a machine) while leaving users uncertain about the next step: how to actually onboard a repository and get a usable brain. Users had to discover entire brain setup as a secondary option, and the documentation did not make clear what prerequisites it needed, what it costs in tokens, what services it installs, or how to control those installations.\nSolution: This branch centralizes the journey around the realistic endpoint—a brain actively working in a user's repository—and breaks it into two clearly-sequenced commands:\nMachine install (scripts/install.sh): Builds and registers two plugins. No repository-specific setup. The README now opens with both commands and states plainly that installing gives no repository a brain.\nRepository onboarding (entire brain setup): A single command that runs in three phases—instant deterministic core (free, seconds), optional fact backfill (token spend, detached, capped at 25 sessions by default), and optional persistent watcher daemon (recurring token spend, launchd agent on macOS / systemd user unit on Linux, installed by default without a prompt).\nThe branch adds four new demo/test scripts and comprehensive documentation clarifying what setup requires (a local git repo, nothing else), what it degrades around (missing entire enable, no captured sessions, no provider), token spend gates and defaults, and paths for both learning (trial-setup.sh, demo-setup.sh, demo-agent-session.sh) and scripting (--no-backfill, --no-daemon). It fixes first-run bugs (JSON parse failures from version banners, missing semantic provider errors, dirty-worktree refusals) and daemon lifecycle issues (duplicate distillation, concurrent setup races, double distillation on re-run). The status command gains an Onboarding section showing backfill progress and watcher health, and the daemon's token spend is now properly gated on per-repo watch cursors instead of a once-per-process budget that would never reset on a long-lived service.",

      "textSnapshot": "Problem: The install and onboarding experience for entire-brain was fragmented. The main README and documentation focused only on installation (getting plugins onto a machine) while leaving users uncertain about the next step: how to actually onboard a repository and get a usable brain. Users had to discover entire brain setup as a secondary option, and the documentation did not make clear what prerequisites it needed, what it costs in tokens, what services it installs, or how to control those installations.\nSolution: This branch centralizes the journey around the realistic endpoint—a brain actively working in a user's repository—and breaks it into two clearly-sequenced commands:\nMachine install (scripts/install.sh): Builds and registers two plugins. No repository-specific setup. The README now opens with both commands and states plainly that installing gives no repository a brain.\nRepository onboarding (entire brain setup): A single command that runs in three phases—instant deterministic core (free, seconds), optional fact backfill (token spend, detached, capped at 25 sessions by default), and optional persistent watcher daemon (recurring token spend, launchd agent on macOS / systemd user unit on Linux, installed by default without a prompt).\nThe branch adds four new demo/test scripts and comprehensive documentation clarifying what setup requires (a local git repo, nothing else), what it degrades around (missing entire enable, no captured sessions, no provider), token spend gates and defaults, and paths for both learning (trial-setup.sh, demo-setup.sh, demo-agent-session.sh) and scripting (--no-backfill, --no-daemon). It fixes first-run bugs (JSON parse failures from version banners, missing semantic provider errors, dirty-worktree refusals) and daemon lifecycle issues (duplicate distillation, concurrent setup races, double distillation on re-run). The status command gains an Onboarding section showing backfill progress and watcher health, and the daemon's token spend is now properly gated on per-repo watch cursors instead of a once-per-process budget that would never reset on a long-lived service.",

      "textSnapshot": "Problem: The install and onboarding experience for entire-brain was fragmented. The main README and documentation focused only on installation (getting plugins onto a machine) while leaving users uncertain about the next step: how to actually onboard a repository and get a usable brain. Users had to discover entire brain setup as a secondary option, and the documentation did not make clear what prerequisites it needed, what it costs in tokens, what services it installs, or how to control those installations.\nSolution: This branch centralizes the journey around the realistic endpoint—a brain actively working in a user's repository—and breaks it into two clearly-sequenced commands:\nMachine install (scripts/install.sh): Builds and registers two plugins. No repository-specific setup. The README now opens with both commands and states plainly that installing gives no repository a brain.\nRepository onboarding (entire brain setup): A single command that runs in three phases—instant deterministic core (free, seconds), optional fact backfill (token spend, detached, capped at 25 sessions by default), and optional persistent watcher daemon (recurring token spend, launchd agent on macOS / systemd user unit on Linux, installed by default without a prompt).\nThe branch adds four new demo/test scripts and comprehensive documentation clarifying what setup requires (a local git repo, nothing else), what it degrades around (missing entire enable, no captured sessions, no provider), token spend gates and defaults, and paths for both learning (trial-setup.sh, demo-setup.sh, demo-agent-session.sh) and scripting (--no-backfill, --no-daemon). It fixes first-run bugs (JSON parse failures from version banners, missing semantic provider errors, dirty-worktree refusals) and daemon lifecycle issues (duplicate distillation, concurrent setup races, double distillation on re-run). The status command gains an Onboarding section showing backfill progress and watcher health, and the daemon's token spend is now properly gated on per-repo watch cursors instead of a once-per-process budget that would never reset on a long-lived service.",
